title: Comparison of surgical outcomes between iStent inject W implantation and microhook ab interno trabeculotomy in combination with phacoemulsification in primary open-angle glaucoma patients

license.statement: CC BY (article <license>: 'Creative Commons Attribution License (CC BY)'; no version number or licence URL given in the XML)

indication: primary open-angle glaucoma (including normal-tension glaucoma eyes) without previous ocular surgery, adults >= 18 years; phacoemulsification combined with an angle procedure; retrospective multicenter comparative case series (Japan)

groups.description: microhook ab interno trabeculotomy (Tanito microhook, about 4 clock hours nasal) combined with phacoemulsification (muLOT-Phaco); n eyes from Table 1 (tab1!R2C2)
iStent inject W (two stents, nasal quadrant) combined with phacoemulsification (iStent-Phaco); n eyes from Table 1 (tab1!R2C3)

exclusions.what: Table 2 'Change from baseline (%)' columns (tab2 C3 and C6)
exclusions.reason: the same table gives absolute IOP; absolute series used (brief rule)

exclusions.what: Table 2 P value columns (C4, C7, C8 with 95% CI)
exclusions.reason: p-values and confidence intervals are not admissible values
success proportions / Kaplan-Meier estimates are not admissible

exclusions.what: Table 3 and Table 4 (number and classes of glaucoma medications)
exclusions.reason: medication counts are not IOP series in schema 1.0.0; mentioned in notes only

exclusions.what: Table 5 postoperative complications (including transient IOP elevation counts)

notes: Reference kind 'preoperative_medicated': Methods state that all glaucoma medications were stopped at the time of surgery (and re-added postoperatively at the surgeon's discretion); Table 1 tabulates the preoperative number of IOP-lowering medications (tab1!R6C2, tab1!R6C3); no washout described.
Tonometer not stated in the article (no Goldmann, rebound or other tonometer named), so method 'unstated'.
Glaucoma medication numbers are tabulated preoperatively (Table 1) and at 3/6/12 months (Table 3); not extracted (schema 1.0.0 has no medication series).
Only the first operated eye per patient was analyzed; surgeon chose the procedure; both arms are standard techniques compared without an investigational agent, so both are 'control' groups.
Surgical failure definition used only for Kaplan-Meier analysis; no outcome-defined analysis set applied to the Table 2 means as far as stated.

series.baseline_label: Baseline row of Table 2 (same cell text as 'Preoperative IOP (mmHg)' in Table 1, tab1!R5C2)
series.notes: Table 2 column 'IOP (mmHg)' under muLOT-Phaco; mean ± SD (Methods: all data expressed as mean ± SD); rows Baseline, Month 3, Month 6, Month 12; per-visit n not tabulated (a minimum 6-month follow-up was an inclusion criterion; the text gives 12-month medication-free eye counts implying fewer eyes at 12 months, ordinary attrition)

series.baseline_label: Baseline row of Table 2 (same cell text as 'Preoperative IOP (mmHg)' in Table 1, tab1!R5C3)
series.notes: Table 2 column 'IOP (mmHg)' under iStent-Phaco; mean ± SD; rows Baseline, Month 3, Month 6, Month 12; per-visit n not tabulated (minimum 6-month follow-up inclusion criterion; fewer eyes at 12 months per text, ordinary attrition)
